profile.headline: AI/LLM Engineer · Available now for senior AI/LLM roles | Production LLM systems: RAG, retrieval, evals, guardrails, cost | 10 years platform & reliability engineering | Python · PHP · Kubernetes
profile.summary:
I spent ten years at Modo Labs, most recently building the admin and configuration layer for Modo My Agent, an LLM assistant deployed across enterprise and university campuses. I'm available now, looking for senior AI/LLM roles, ideally evals or agent infrastructure.

Part of that was the layer where customers connect their Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to the assistant, including a per-environment tool catalog with live refresh. I built the admin UI for four connectors (LDAP, D2L Brightspace, Ellucian Banner, internal messaging) and verified each contract from the retrieval backend's source. I also shipped the safety-notification configuration, with a legally gated enablement control.

I released package updates every two weeks as Release Engineer for the Core team. A typical release morning covered seven repositories: 13 pull requests, 12 tags, and four container channel promotions. I introduced an adversarial pre-merge review practice that the engineering lead adopted.

I build at home too. Steward, my MCP server, gives an LLM assistant 18 tools over the personal-finance platform I self-host; I've used it daily since July 2026. My family's shopping list and pantry run on an app I built and host myself, with an English and German voice interface we use from our phones. An OpenAI-compatible local model keeps bulk classification off metered APIs.

I'm bilingual in English and Spanish, and open to remote or hybrid around Boston and Cambridge.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Most recently I built the admin and configuration layer for Modo My Agent, an LLM assistant deployed across enterprise and university campuses, from MCP server configuration to per-turn telemetry, on a PHP and Kubernetes platform.

• Shipped the configuration layer for customer Model Context Protocol servers: identifier validation and a per-environment tool catalog with live refresh.
• Built the admin UI for configuring four assistant integration connectors: LDAP with raw filters, D2L Brightspace, Ellucian Banner, and internal messaging.
• Delivered the safety-notification configuration: recipient lists with deploy reconciliation, canned-response safety fields, and a legally gated enablement control.
• Released package updates every two weeks as Release Engineer for the Core team. A typical release morning covered seven repositories: 13 pull requests, 12 tags, and four container channel promotions. Corrected a release gate that had dropped a repository from a coordinated version cut.
• Built a correctness gate that runs before code goes up and back-tested it blind on six of a colleague's pull requests rewound to the commit their reviewer first saw, catching all five bugs the reviewer found plus two that had merged.
• Drove AI-assisted debugging of production defects and reported them fast, with proof - on one image bug, Claude checked the image files in S3 and found one was public and one was private. It tracked down when that change started, which helped address the problem much more quickly.
• Introduced an adversarial pre-merge review practice that the engineering lead adopted, catching refactor regressions that both automated reviewers and earlier human passes missed.
positions.insights: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Prompt Engineering and +4 skills

positions.title: Web Integration Developer
positions.description: Built and maintained customer-facing web integrations connecting external data sources into the app platform, then grew from integration work into core platform engineering.

positions.title: Data Center Operations Technician
positions.description: Provided multilingual (English and Spanish) technical support for companies that contracted with Support.com (such as Comcast, SMC) by effectively troubleshooting customer internet and home security issues while following specific QA guidelines with a friendly and courteous attitude. Frequently scored >90% QA score while the floor averaged 60%, and received near perfect ratings from customers.

positions.title: Security Analyst
positions.description: Participated on the UConn SecureU project. The objective was to remediate Personally Identifiable Information on UConn computers by either securing it or shredding it if it was not needed. Worked extensively with Splunk (Indexing software) and Identity Finder (PII Remediation software). Worked extensively on web development using HTML, CSS, and PHP. Used Linux extensively.

positions.title: Database Manager
positions.description: Created forms and reports using Microsoft Access for UITS Business Office faculty, using SQL queries extensively. Designed, planned, and converted Access database over to an Oracle database, rolling out changes to the entire office in a short time span.

positions.title: CIO Intern
positions.description:
As a CIO Intern at IBM I worked in the HR division that is responsible for tracking all employee information within the company. I was assigned an excellent mentor who assisted and guided me, and was placed in a Data Migration team where I was assigned tasks that would help the team through the process of upgrading their internal HR systems. I worked closely with my team and participated in weekly conference calls in order to update the team on my progress. My roles while working in the Data Migration team were to:

- Quickly learn how to make use of new technologies, specifically IBM's InfoSphere DataStage software to create job sequences that would fulfill the necessary requirements.
- Developed complex functional job sequences from scratch that consisted of parallel running tasks (multitasking) and worked extensively to make them more efficient.
- Extensively used SQL to collect data from several internal databases and improved several previously developed job sequences by making them more efficient and robust.

volunteerExperiences.description: After graduating from Fitch High School in 2009, I returned to mentor the robotics team at the school for two years. As a team mentor, I helped the team plan for the competition, helped keep things organized, and focused on helping to educate and train the programming group.

projects.description:

       • The application is published on the Android market and holds over 1200 active device installs and a rating of 5 stars
